blocks.content: 1. Genetics – Introduction

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Gregor Mendel discovered the fundamental principles of inheritance through his experiments on garden pea plants (Pisum sativum).
Mendel formulated three laws of inheritance: Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation, and Law of Independent Assortment.
Genes are the basic functional units of heredity located on chromosomes and are composed of DNA.
Humans possess 23 pairs of chromosomes, including 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes (XX in females, XY in males).
Sex determination in humans is paternal, as the male sperm carries either an X or a Y chromosome to determine offspring sex.

blocks.content:
Genetics is the branch of biology that deals with the study of heredity and variation.

It explains how traits are passed from parents to offspring.

Genetics helps in understanding similarities and differences among individuals.

The science of genetics plays an important role in agriculture, medicine, and evolution.

The foundation of genetics was laid by Gregor Mendel through his experiments on pea plants.

Modern genetics is based on genes, DNA, and chromosomes.
2. Heredity – Meaning

Heredity is the transmission of genetic characters from parents to offspring.

Characters such as height, eye color, skin color, and blood group are inherited.

Heredity ensures continuity of species.

It is responsible for resemblance between parents and their children.

Heredity works through genes present on chromosomes.

Environmental factors may influence expression of inherited traits.
3. Variation

Variation refers to differences among individuals of the same species.

Variations may be genetic or environmental.

Genetic variations are inherited from parents.

Environmental variations are caused by surroundings.

Variation helps organisms adapt to changing environment.

It is the basis of evolution and natural selection.
4. Gregor Mendel – Father of Genetics

Gregor Mendel is known as the Father of Genetics.

He conducted experiments on garden pea plants.

Mendel selected pea plants because they show clear contrasting traits.

His experiments explained inheritance patterns.

Mendel proposed laws of inheritance based on his observations.

His work laid foundation of modern genetics.
5. Mendel’s Experiment

Mendel selected seven pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants.

Examples include tall and dwarf plants, round and wrinkled seeds.

He crossed pure-breeding plants.

He observed inheritance of traits in different generations.

Based on results, Mendel proposed laws of inheritance.
6. Mendel’s Law of Dominance
Gregor Mendel is universally recognized as the Father of Genetics.

According to the law of dominance, one character dominates over the other.

The dominant trait is expressed in the first generation.

The recessive trait remains hidden.

For example, tallness is dominant over dwarfness.

Dominant allele is represented by capital letter.

Recessive allele is represented by small letter.
7. Mendel’s Law of Segregation

The law of segregation states that alleles separate during gamete formation.

Each gamete receives only one allele.

This separation occurs during meiosis.

The law is also called law of purity of gametes.

It explains reappearance of recessive trait in F2 generation.
8. Mendel’s Law of Independent Assortment

This law states that inheritance of one trait is independent of another.

It applies when genes are located on different chromosomes.

Traits are assorted independently during gamete formation.

This law explains inheritance of two traits together.

Example includes seed shape and seed color in peas.
9. Monohybrid Cross

A monohybrid cross involves inheritance of one trait.

Mendel crossed tall and dwarf pea plants.

All F1 generation plants were tall.

In F2 generation, ratio was 3:1.

Genotypic ratio was 1:2:1.

This cross explains dominance and segregation.
10. Dihybrid Cross

A dihybrid cross involves inheritance of two traits.

Mendel crossed round yellow seeds with wrinkled green seeds.

F1 generation showed round yellow seeds.

F2 generation showed 9:3:3:1 ratio.

This cross explains independent assortment of traits.
11. Gene – Definition

A gene is the functional unit of heredity.

Genes are segments of DNA.

They carry information for synthesis of proteins.

Genes control expression of traits.

Genes are located on chromosomes.

Each trait is controlled by a pair of genes.
12. Chromosomes

Chromosomes are thread-like structures found in nucleus.

They are composed of DNA and proteins.

Chromosomes carry genes.

Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes.

Autosomes and sex chromosomes are two types.

Chromosome number is constant for a species.
13. DNA – Genetic Material

DNA stands for Deoxyribonucleic Acid.

It is the genetic material in most organisms.

DNA carries genetic information.

It has a double helix structure.

DNA replicates during cell division.

DNA controls synthesis of proteins.

items: Monohybrid Cross ratios: Phenotypic ratio is 3:1, Genotypic ratio is 1:2:1.
Dihybrid Cross Phenotypic ratio is strictly 9:3:3:1.
Down Syndrome is caused by the trisomy of chromosome 21, resulting in 47 total chromosomes.
Haemophilia and Color Blindness are frequently asked X-linked recessive genetic disorders.

blocks.content: 14. Sex Determination in Humans

Sex determination refers to determination of sex of child.

In humans, sex is determined by X and Y chromosomes.

Female has XX chromosomes.

Male has XY chromosomes.

Father determines the sex of child.

This system is called XY type sex determination.
15. Genetic Disorders

Genetic disorders are caused by abnormal genes or chromosomes.

Examples include color blindness and hemophilia.

These disorders are inherited.

Some disorders are sex-linked.

Genetic counseling helps in prevention.

Early diagnosis is important.
16. IMPORTANT FACTS – SSC FOCUS

• Genetics is study of heredity.

• Gregor Mendel is father of genetics.

• Gene is unit of heredity.

• Law of dominance explains dominant traits.

• Law of segregation is purity of gametes.

• Monohybrid ratio is 3:1.

• Dihybrid ratio is 9:3:3:1.

• Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes.

• DNA is genetic material.

• Father determines sex of child.
